definition: A Rust Policy is a pure native strategy selector. It calls separately generated declared Rules with explicit borrowed inputs, evaluates authored cases in order and returns a typed target identity without importing or executing the target.
strategy: Each Policy owns an enum whose variants are collision-free encodings of the qualified Operation or Calculation targets. The enum exposes the exact DomainSpec selector as inert identity.
evaluation: Cases retain authored occurrence order, including repeated targets or Rules. Evaluation stops at the first true Rule and otherwise returns the declared default target.
dependencies: Every Rule call is qualified through the checked Rust Rule module and binds exactly the declared typed arguments. Target modules are never dependencies of Policy code.
ownership: Policy inputs are immutably borrowed; temporary literal or collection arguments live only for the Rule call. The returned strategy enum is Copy and contains no executable capability.
module: One collision-free module per qualified selector under src/domain/policies. Required Rule artifacts are included as an exact dependency closure.
verification: Deterministic planning, Cargo execution for ordered and default branches, target non-execution evidence and wrong-strategy compile-fail controls are required.
compatibility: Legacy inline-predicate Policy remains unchanged on existing paths. This candidate requires v2 named Rules and has no default cutover.
